issues.legal_issue: Standing trees forming part of a grove cannot be separately attached in execution of a mortgage decree after the former intermediary rights have vested and new tenure rights have arisen.
material_facts: The creditor sought to attach standing trees in groves during execution of a mortgage decree after the statutory vesting of the former intermediary rights.

The earlier decision in the same dispute had held that the former rights were extinguished, new tenure rights arose, and the mortgagee could pursue the compensation awarded to the intermediary rather than sell those new rights.
The lower courts allowed execution against the trees on the ground that trees could be distinguished from grove land.
issues.conclusion: Standing uncut trees in a grove form part of grove land and cannot be separately attached in execution of the mortgage decree. The mortgagee may pursue the compensation awarded to the intermediary through the applicable statutory route, but not the newly created tenure rights.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3(13) and 6(a)(i) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, an intermediary’s grove is grove land and the relevant rights vest in the State free from encumbrances; section 18(1)(a) treats the intermediary’s grove as bhumidhari property. Standing uncut trees are part of the land, and an inseparable part is included in the whole. The Court followed its earlier decision in Rana Sheo Ambar Singh v. Allahabad Bank Ltd., 1962 (2) SCR 441, that the mortgagee’s remedy after vesting is under section 6(h) of the Act read with section 73 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, against the compensation awarded to the intermediary, not the newly created tenure rights.

rule.if: mortgage_decree_execution and enforcement_after_rights_vested and standing_uncut_trees_in_grove and grove_part_of_new_tenure_rights

predicates.mortgage_decree_execution: A creditor sought to enforce a mortgage decree through execution proceedings.
predicates.enforcement_after_rights_vested: The creditor sought enforcement after the former intermediary rights had vested and new tenure rights had arisen.
predicates.standing_uncut_trees_in_grove: The property targeted in execution consisted of standing, uncut trees forming part of a grove.
predicates.grove_part_of_new_tenure_rights: The grove was included in the newly created tenure rights.

issues.definition: When a creditor seeks execution of a mortgage decree after former rights have vested, and the targeted standing trees are part of a grove included in new tenure rights, those trees cannot be separately attached in that execution.
